title: Gifts for coffee lovers UK 2026: 10 machines and gadgets from £49
seoTitle: Gifts for Coffee Lovers UK 2026: From £49 to Splurge
description: Gifts for coffee lovers at UK Black Friday prices: De'Longhi Magnifica Evo Next £379, Lavazza frother £49, Ninja DualBrew £169.99 and more.
intro:
**Our best gift for a coffee lover is the De'Longhi Magnifica Evo Next bean-to-cup machine at £379 on Amazon, £220 off. Best cheap pick: the Lavazza MilkEasy Plus milk frother at £49. Best splurge: a Rocket Espresso Appartamento 2.0 at £1,390.**

Every price below comes from UK retailers and deal roundups dated 21 or 22 November 2026, during Black Friday Week. Prices move fast, so check before you buy.

deals.name: Lavazza MilkEasy Plus milk frother
deals.note: Our best cheap pick: hot or cold foam for lattes and cappuccinos, and it makes a decent hot chocolate too. Works with any coffee machine, so it's a safe gift for someone who already owns one (TechRadar, 22 November).

deals.name: Nespresso Vertuo Pop
deals.note: Half price from £49 at John Lewis (and Currys) on 22 November; some colours cost a few pounds more. Easiest machine on the list, but pods cost more per cup than beans over time.

deals.name: Lavazza Tabli tab coffee machine
deals.note: Uses compressed coffee 'tabs' instead of pods, so there's far less packaging to throw away. Half price at Amazon (TechRadar, 22 November). Tabs are only sold by Lavazza, so check they're easy to get before you buy.

deals.name: Ninja Prestige DualBrew
deals.note: Makes espresso-style shots from pods and a full jug of filter coffee from grounds, with a built-in frother. £90 off (TechRadar, 22 November) and cheaper than last year's Cyber Monday price of about £208.

deals.name: Philips Baristina espresso machine
deals.note: A compact bean-to-cup that grinds, tamps and brews with one swipe of the handle. £50 off at Amazon (TechRadar, 22 November), with John Lewis matching it. Pair it with the Lavazza frother for milky drinks.

deals.name: De'Longhi La Specialista Arte
deals.note: A manual espresso machine with a built-in grinder and steam wand, for someone who wants to learn latte art. £329 at Amazon (TechRadar, 22 November), below last Cyber Monday's £349.

deals.name: Sage the Bambino Plus
deals.note: The easiest proper espresso machine to learn on, with automatic milk texturing. Needs ground coffee or a separate grinder. £349 at Amazon (TechRadar, 21 November); it was about £329 last Black Friday.

deals.name: De'Longhi Magnifica Evo Next bean-to-cup
deals.note: Our best overall: grinds fresh beans and froths milk at the press of a button, so the whole household can use it. £220 off at Amazon (TechRadar, 21 and 22 November).

deals.name: Sage the Barista Express
deals.note: The classic first 'proper' home espresso machine, with a built-in grinder. £499.99 at Currys (TechRadar, 22 November), but Amazon charged £449 last Black Friday, so check the Amazon link and aim for £449 to £479.

deals.name: Rocket Espresso Appartamento 2.0 Serie Nera
deals.note: Our best splurge: a hand-built Italian heat-exchanger machine that will outlast every gadget on this list. Full price from Rocket's official UK store on 22 November, with free two-person delivery. Needs a good grinder.

body:
## Best gifts for coffee lovers at a glance

- **Best overall:** De'Longhi Magnifica Evo Next, £379 at Amazon
- **Best cheap:** Lavazza MilkEasy Plus milk frother, £49 at Amazon
- **Best splurge:** Rocket Espresso Appartamento 2.0, £1,390 at Rocket Espresso
- **Best for beginners:** Sage the Bambino Plus, £349 at Amazon
- **Best for filter and espresso:** Ninja Prestige DualBrew, £169.99 at Amazon

## How to choose a gift for a coffee lover

Start with what they drink now. Someone who buys a flat white every morning wants milk, so a bean-to-cup machine or a frother will change their life. Someone who drinks black filter coffee won't care about a steam wand but will love a machine that makes a full jug. And a home barista who already owns a good machine is best left alone: get them an accessory, a bag of good beans or a frother rather than a second machine.

Next, think about effort. **Bean-to-cup** machines like the De'Longhi Magnifica Evo Next and Philips Baristina do everything at a touch, which suits a busy household. **Manual espresso** machines like the Sage Bambino Plus and De'Longhi La Specialista Arte make better coffee once you've learned them, but need a few weeks of practice. **Pod and tab** machines (Nespresso, Lavazza Tabli) are the easiest of all, but each cup costs more over time.

## Which machines are worth it this Christmas?

The **Magnifica Evo Next at £379** is the safest big present: it's £220 off and anyone can use it. If space is tight, the **Baristina** at £249.99 is smaller but has no milk wand, so add the £49 Lavazza frother.

For someone who likes a hobby, the **Bambino Plus** (£349) or **La Specialista Arte** (£329) are the picks. The Sage is easier to learn, while the De'Longhi has a grinder built in, so it's better value if they don't own one.

The **Ninja DualBrew** at £169.99 is the most flexible: proper filter coffee for a crowd at the weekend and quick pod shots on weekdays.

At the top, a **Rocket Appartamento** is the gift for a coffee obsessive. It's never discounted much, but it's built to be repaired rather than replaced. Read our [Rocket Espresso Appartamento vs Mozzafiato guide](/guides/rocket-espresso-machine-review/) before you buy.

## Good prices to aim for

From last year's Black Friday and this week's prices: under £400 for the Magnifica Evo Next, about £330 to £350 for the Bambino Plus, under £250 for the Baristina and about £450 to £480 for the Barista Express. Pod machines like the Vertuo Pop are worth buying at £50 or less. Every machine is compared in more detail in our [coffee machine Black Friday guide](/guides/coffee-machine-black-friday-deals-2026/).

Most Amazon prices here run until Cyber Monday (30 November). Some Black Friday prices need Prime; a [Prime free trial](https://www.amazon.co.uk/amazonprime) also gets the machine delivered quickly. More ideas are in our [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/).

## FAQs

### What is a good gift for a coffee lover who has everything?

An upgrade to how they make milk drinks, such as the Lavazza MilkEasy Plus frother at £49, or a gift card for a speciality coffee subscription. Only buy a new machine if theirs is old or basic.

### Is a bean-to-cup machine better than a pod machine?

For a daily coffee drinker, usually yes. Beans cost far less per cup than pods, and the coffee tastes fresher. Pod machines are cheaper to buy and simpler, so they suit occasional drinkers.

### What is the best coffee machine for a beginner?

The Sage Bambino Plus. It heats up in seconds and textures milk automatically, so learning espresso is much less frustrating. A bean-to-cup like the Magnifica Evo Next is easier still if they don't want to learn at all.

### Do I need a grinder with an espresso machine?

Yes for the Sage Bambino Plus, Barista-style machines and the Rocket, unless you buy pre-ground coffee, which goes stale quickly. The De'Longhi La Specialista Arte and the bean-to-cup machines have grinders built in.

### When is the best time to buy a coffee machine?

Black Friday Week, which runs to Cyber Monday on 30 November, is usually the cheapest time of year. Prices often go back up in December.
